test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 10 Feb, 2026 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
In the given figure, AB is parallel to CD. Angle PAB = 70 degrees and angle APC = 30 degrees. What is the value (in degrees) of angle DCP ?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fab974df1c3c30893e6afe81540cc7794adf13a63ddefd5c876fa2945d0495fb.png]
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Extend the line segment PC to intersect the parallel line AB at point Q.

Applying the exterior angle theorem to ▵PAQ, the exterior angle at Q is the sum of opposite interior angles.

Exterior ∠PQB = ∠PAB + ∠APC = 70° + 30° = 100°.

Since AB || CD, the corresponding angles ∠DCP and ∠PQB are equal.

**∴ The correct answer is 100°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: AB || CD, ∠PAB = 70°, ∠APC = 30°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2bd8b1c34ae73948afde90ab51c9977fedbb85ccbd508b5b87aa40e96d105979.png] 

Construction: Extend PC to meet AB at point Q.

⇒ In ▵PAQ, ∠PAQ = 70° and ∠APQ = 30°.

⇒ ∠PQA = 180° − (∠PAQ + ∠APQ)

⇒ ∠PQA = 180° − (70° + 30°) = 80°.

⇒ ∠PQB = 180° − ∠PQA = 180° − 80° = 100°.

⇒ Since AB || CD and PCQ is a transversal, ∠DCP = ∠PQB (Corresponding angles).

⇒ ∠DCP = 100°.

**∴ The correct answer is 100°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Parallel Lines and Transversals

When two parallel lines are cut by a transversal, corresponding angles are equal, and alternate interior angles are equal.

Exterior Angle Theorem

The exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the two opposite interior angles (∠Ext = ∠Int₁ + ∠Int₂).

Angle Sum Property

The sum of all interior angles in any triangle is always exactly 180°.
